passage:
After a typhoon damaged phone networks, a small community radio station became important. It shared shelter locations, road closures, and messages from families.
Many young people had never listened to it before. They discovered that local radio could work when online systems failed.
The station later invited students to produce emergency information segments.
Students learned that media resilience matters. A community should not depend on only one communication channel.
Old technology may seem outdated during normal days. During crisis, it can become a lifeline.
A strong information system has backups, local knowledge, and voices people trust.
